tags.name: admin_api
tags.description: The admin page's API. Administrators only (there is no delegation: this page can turn protection off and lift blocks). Every change needs a recent password confirmation and is written to the audit log.

tags.name: approval
tags.description: Requests for the approval of a second administrator: the list, and the decisions (also the actions of the approval notification). Administrators only (the default for controllers) and CSRF-protected. A decision needs a recent password confirmation; the rules who may decide are in {@see ApprovalService}, shared with occ. Approving also needs the deciding administrator's own login to have been confirmed when it needed a confirmation: a session that was let in without one must not let others in.

tags.name: blocklist_api
tags.description: The firewall export and the blocklists on the Blocks tab. Administrators only; every change needs a recent password confirmation and is audited. The export directory is deliberately not settable here: it is read from config.php only, so a web administrator cannot make Nextcloud write files anywhere on the server.

tags.name: confirmation_api
tags.description: Login confirmation on the admin page. Its settings are changed through the settings endpoint or, for the outcomes of all reasons at once, the preset endpoint; waiting logins are decided through the approvals endpoints. Every change needs password confirmation. Administrators only.

tags.name: decoy_api
tags.description: The Decoys tab: decoy credentials, reserved names and trap paths. Administrators only; every change needs a recent password confirmation and is audited. The secret of a decoy is returned once, by the request that creates it, and never stored: no endpoint can return it again.

tags.name: digest_api
tags.description: The admin page's API for the digest email. Administrators only, like the rest of the admin API.

tags.name: events_api
tags.description: The admin page's API for the typed events that webhooks can receive. Administrators only, like the rest of the admin API.

tags.name: incident_api
tags.description: The incident report on the Incidents tab. Administrators only. A report reveals what Nextcloud knows about an account or an address, so every way to get one needs a recent password confirmation, is rate limited and written to the audit log. Downloads are POST requests that answer with the document itself: the page fetches it with its CSRF token and password confirmation, then saves or prints it. No link, ticket or copy of the report exists on the server afterwards.

tags.name: learning_action
tags.description: The actions of the "learning period ends tomorrow" notification. Administrators only (the default for controllers), CSRF-protected, and idempotent: they act only while that notice is pending. A notification action cannot ask for the password, which is why both actions do only what the notice offered and are written to the audit log.

tags.name: notification_api
tags.description: The Notifications tab. Administrators only. The settings themselves are changed through the settings endpoint of the admin API.

tags.name: payload_api
tags.description: The signatures of the injection probe check and "Test a URL". Administrators only. Nothing here changes anything: signatures are switched and added through the check's settings, and the tests run the matcher on the server without sending a request or recording anything. They take a body because the input can be long, and are rate limited because they run regular expressions.

tags.name: personal_api
tags.description: The logged-in user's own security events, their answers to "Was this you?" (also the actions of the user notification), their trusted networks, their remembered devices, their recent logins, the overview at the top of their security section, their recent activity and "Log out everywhere else" (concept sections 11.5.1, 11.8 and 15.1). Every endpoint only ever touches the current user's own rows: another account's detection or network answers 404, like a missing one. Writes are CSRF-protected (OCS) and rate limited per user; "Yes, it was me" needs a recent password confirmation and is refused from the session the detection is about.

tags.name: privacy_api
tags.description: The "Data and privacy" tab. Administrators only.

tags.name: secure_account_admin
tags.description: The "Secure my account" state of a detection's account on the admin page (concept sections 11.15 and 15.3): the checklist's progress, and for accounts locked with the lock link "Re-enable and start Secure my * account". Administrators only; every write needs password confirmation and is audited.

tags.name: share_alert
tags.description: The "Disable link" action of the notification that tells someone the password of their share is being guessed.

tags.name: simulation_api
tags.description: "Simulate" on the check cards. Administrators only. A simulation only reads the settings: nothing is recorded, blocked or notified.
